(Search-snippet content — full article 403'd on direct fetch; CNBC's own reporting language, 20 July 2026)

Brent crude futures were trading at $88.01 per barrel, after prices jumped nearly 4% overnight
to break $90 per barrel following confirmation that at least three US service members died
during recent fighting. US West Texas Intermediate crude fell 25 cents to $82.24 per barrel.

Oil prices turned lower Monday after Iran said negotiations with the US could be pursued based
on Tehran's interests, raising hopes that diplomacy could end the escalation.

Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei told reporters that intermediaries had
continued to exchange messages with Tehran during the latest round of US strikes, suggesting
diplomatic channels remain open.

The US has bombed Iran for nine consecutive nights in retaliation for repeated attacks on oil
tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said
Iran had suspended its commitments to the memorandum of understanding signed last month.

Separately (CNBC, 20 July): Houthi militants in Yemen declared a maritime embargo against Saudi
Arabia effective immediately, threatening to exacerbate supply disruption. The average US price
for a gallon of gas hit $4 on Monday.
